LG 2.1 soundbar. Uses NECx1 protocol (device 44, subdevice 44). Full IR codes in irdb (codes/LG/Sound Bar/44,44.csv). Remote AKB73575401, shared across 30+ LG NB-series soundbars. LG is listed under Audio / AV Receiver in the cloud catalog.
Sharp AC already fully supported with dedicated protocol family. CRMC is Sharp's standard remote prefix.
TCL 3-Series Roku TV. TCL TV packs for IR, Roku packs for navigation. Also supports Wi-Fi control via Roku ECP protocol.
Mitsubishi Electric protocol already in cloud catalog. MSY=indoor, MUY=outdoor unit. Standard 18-byte protocol, 38kHz.
Sharp AC family already supported. The AH-AxSAY series uses Sharp's CRMC-A907JBEZ remote protocol.
SU.YOSO sells the HY300 Pro projector made by Magcubic. Two HY300 remote code sets added under Magcubic (search SU.YOSO or Magcubic).
Hisense TVs already supported with 160+ code sets, mostly exact captures from the IRext database. VIM is not a known Hisense model; searching VIDAA also finds Hisense.
Windows PC control isn't supported yet: laptops have no IR receiver and the app has no PC companion protocol. Logged to gauge demand for PC control.

Sold in Indonesia as the SMOON HY 320 — the same HY300-family Android projector Magcubic and SU.YOSO rebadge. Smoon added as an alias of Magcubic, so the two HY300 remote code sets now come up when searching Smoon. Unverified against the actual unit.

Already supported. Haier split units run on the computed Haier family, which sends the 176-bit, 160-bit and YR-W02 112-bit frames in a single press, so it drives an HSU wall unit whichever YR-series remote it shipped with. 205 Haier code sets are also published. No change needed; unverified against this unit.

Eolia F-series, remote ACXF00-14780. Asked twice (2026-09-14, 2026-09-16, the second from 1.4.1). IR is not a route and will not be: the 21 Panasonic AC packs we hold are all export A75C-family captures, Flipper-IRDB's five Panasonic AC files hold no ACXF00, and IRremoteESP8266 — the reference for this protocol — implements only NKE, DKE, JKE, CKP and RKR, every one identified by an A75C or CS- remote. The Japanese domestic Eolia framing has no public encoder to build a family from.

Comfort Cloud is the only way to drive this unit, and two things had to be true. The Auth0 sign-in rewrite (3e29323) is in v1.5-b2, so that part already shipped. But AddDeviceConfigView.transportOptions never listed .panasonic — nor MELCloud, ThinQ, SmartHQ, De'Longhi, Sensibo, SmartThings, ConnectLife or SwitchBot — so the transport could not be selected at all. Fixed in c9b1ab0, held for the next release. Until that build ships there is nothing this customer can do, and the transport has still never been run against a real account.

AMX100 is a white-label mini Android projector also sold as Sainellor, Amovfilm and AimeiSen; no capture exists for it in Flipper-IRDB or irdb under any of those names. LEC added as an alias of the generic captures, and those six sets now also surface under the name Generic instead of only BrandUnknown. Whether they drive an AMX100 is unverified — learning the remote is the reliable path.

Asked twice (2026-09-16, both in Japanese; the second spelled the brand アイリスオオヤマ, which the searchTerms already cover). R5.0-D is the remote, not the light: it ships with the LED ceiling lights of the 5.0 series (CL6D-5.0 and siblings) and Iris Ohyama now sells CL-RL1 as its replacement; R5.0-DL / CL-RL2 are the colour-temperature variants. No code set exists for it anywhere public — Flipper-IRDB has no Iris Ohyama entry and no Japanese ceiling light at all, irdb has no such brand, and the one project that drives this exact remote (Akkiesoft/airpippi, config/R5.0-DL) keeps its ir-ctl captures outside the repo. The brand row now also carries the light category and the remote's model numbers, so the picker and search reach it; learning the remote through an IR bridge is still the only working path. The earlier note here blamed export_irext.py's MIN_KEYS floor for the missing lights — that was wrong and is corrected in CLAUDE.md: the irext index holds 13 light rows in total, 10 already imported, and the floor is now 1 anyway.

Non-smart 1080p US set (its own quick-start manual lists no Wi-Fi or smart features; remote EN-22655S), so it is IR only — no Roku or network transport applies despite the Roku-era Q naming. Sharp was already in the picker, but the curated pack it leads to, sharp-tv-01, held generic NEC numbers tagged as the Sharp protocol: Power sent OBC 1, the digit "1". Rebuilt from the canonical Sharp map (address 1, plus Sharp's second device 17 for transport and discrete power), 12 buttons to 48, verified bit-for-bit against the Flipper captures we ship. Published as v2 in manifest v28, so installed builds pick it up. Not tested on a Sharp TV. Request arrived in Spanish, no region given.
